nodes.name: auth_audit
nodes.task:
Security-audit the authentication/session implementation in server/auth.ts (with server/config.ts, server/users.ts and contracts/users.json as supporting context only if relevant) and write the findings to reports/auth.md. This is an assessment deliverable only: do NOT modify application source, config, contracts, or tests — the only file you create/change is reports/auth.md.

Scope: identify authentication and session-expiry vulnerabilities, e.g. missing or ineffective expiry enforcement, tokens/sessions that remain valid after expiry or logout, credential or secret comparison weaknesses, predictable/insufficiently random session identifiers, timing or enumeration leaks, missing validation of session ownership, and unsafe defaults around expiry configuration. Read the actual implementation to decide which of these apply; do not assert a vulnerability you cannot point to in the code.

For each finding, reports/auth.md must contain: a short title, severity (critical/high/medium/low) with a one-line justification, exact file/line evidence quoted from server/auth.ts, a concrete reproduction case (a described attack sequence, or a small reproduction snippet/command that is actually run against the repository where feasible — record the real command and its real exit status/output), the impact if exploited, and a recommended fix described at the design level (no code is to be implemented). Where the code's intent is ambiguous or a contract does not define the behavior, state that as an interpretation/open question rather than inventing a stricter requirement.

End the file with a summary table of findings by severity and an explicit statement of which findings you consider release-blocking. Verification: reports/auth.md exists, every finding cites real server/auth.ts evidence, and no application source files were altered.

nodes.name: storage_audit
nodes.task:
Reliability-audit the persistence layer in server/storage.ts and write the findings to reports/storage.md. This is an assessment deliverable only: do NOT modify application source, config, contracts, or tests — the only file you create/change is reports/storage.md.

Scope: crash-consistency and data-loss risks — non-atomic writes (truncate-then-write vs write-temp-then-rename), missing fsync of file and/or parent directory, absent or incomplete recovery from a partially written state on startup, unhandled write/read errors that silently drop data, lost-update or corruption risk from concurrent access, unsafe deletion/overwrite ordering, and path or encoding issues that could destroy existing stored data. Determine which of these actually apply by reading the implementation; do not claim a risk without code evidence.

For each finding, reports/storage.md must contain: a short title, severity with one-line justification, exact file/line evidence quoted from server/storage.ts, a concrete failure scenario (the interleaving or crash point that triggers it, plus how it would be reproduced or observed — prefer a small deterministic reproduction or failure injection over probabilistic disk experiments, and record the actual command run and its real output/exit status), the data-loss or corruption impact, and a recommended fix at the design level (no code is to be implemented). Mark anything the code leaves undefined as an interpretation/open question.

End the file with a summary table of findings by severity and an explicit statement of which findings you consider release-blocking. Verification: reports/storage.md exists, each scenario is grounded in real server/storage.ts code, and no application source files were altered.

nodes.name: release_assessment
nodes.task:
Write reports/release.md: a release-readiness assessment for this service, synthesized from reports/auth.md and reports/storage.md (produced by the completed auth and storage audits). Assessment only — do NOT modify application source, config, contracts, or tests; the only file you create is reports/release.md.

Content requirements:
1) Release decision up front (release / release with documented risk / block), with the conditions that would change it.
2) Prioritized blocker list: take the findings marked release-blocking in both reports, rank them by combined severity and exploit/recovery likelihood, and cite the corresponding sections of reports/auth.md and reports/storage.md rather than re-deriving the analysis.
3) Tradeoffs: for each blocker, the cost and behavioral impact of the recommended fix versus shipping with the risk (including any public-behavior or compatibility implications — the workspace README asks that existing public behavior be kept unless the user requests a change).
4) Explicitly reconcile any contradictions between the two reports; if a finding's evidence is missing, unsupported, or its severity looks inconsistent with the cited code, call that out in a "Report quality gaps" section instead of silently reinterpreting it. Do not perform new source audits beyond what is needed to check the reports' claims.
5) Verification evidence: record the actual commands you ran to confirm the reports' claims or reproduce cited cases, with their real exit codes, and clearly separate observed facts from inferences.
6) Recommended fix ordering / follow-up work items (design level only; no implementation).

Verification: reports/release.md exists, references both audit reports by section, states a single clear release recommendation, and no application source files were altered.

nodes.name: reports_integrity_review
nodes.task:
Perform a final consistency and integrity check on the release assessment deliverables in reports/auth.md, reports/storage.md, and reports/release.md, and record the result in reports/README.md (a short index plus the verification verdict). You own these report files: you may correct them directly — fix mis-cited line references, remove or downgrade findings whose evidence does not hold, restore missing required sections (severity, evidence, reproduction scenario, recommended fix), and repair cross-references so that every blocker listed in reports/release.md traces to an actual finding in an audit report.

Checks to perform:
1) Every quoted code snippet and file/line reference in the two audit reports matches the current content of server/auth.ts and server/storage.ts. Re-read those files to confirm the cited constructs exist as described.
2) Each audit finding has severity, evidence, a concrete reproduction or failure scenario, impact, and a design-level recommended fix; the release report has a single explicit release recommendation, a prioritized blocker list, and a tradeoffs section.
3) Reproduction commands recorded in the reports are safe, read-only, bounded re-executions (or explicitly noted as not re-run, with the reason); report their real exit codes.
4) Strict constraint: application source must not be changed. Do not edit anything outside reports/, and do not implement any recommended fix. Note: worktrees do not expose the original checkout, so verify this by inspection (source files still contain the constructs the reports cite, and no fix code was added) rather than by comparing with a base commit or relying on git status/diff.

If an audit finding is unsupportable, delete it from the audit report and update the blocker list and release recommendation in reports/release.md accordingly; keep the overall release conclusion consistent across the three files. Do not launch a new full source audit or duplicate the original security/reliability analysis.

Final line of reports/README.md: <ACCEPT> if the assessment is complete, internally consistent, and no application source was modified; otherwise fix what you own, re-run the checks, and if a defect remains outside your authority (e.g. application source was altered or an entire audit deliverable is missing), state the specific problem and end with <REVISE>.

originalGoal: Assess whether this service is ready for release without changing application source. Audit server/auth.ts for authentication/session expiry vulnerabilities and write reports/auth.md with evidence, reproduction cases, severity and recommended fixes. Separately audit server/storage.ts for crash consistency and data-loss risks and write reports/storage.md with failure scenarios, severity and recommended fixes. Produce reports/release.md using both reports to prioritize blockers, explain tradeoffs and recommend a release decision. Do not implement the fixes in this assessment.
